gap_text: The two Dagu records disagree on dashboard authentication. The hosting receipt (2026-09-19) records basic auth with anonymous 401 and authenticated 200 after restart. The current hosting README says the dashboard now uses upstream auth.mode none, with anonymous API reads returning 200. No retained receipt covers the current auth mode.
next_check: Against the running dagu-equities service, send an anonymous and an authenticated `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` request to the dashboard API. Record the configured auth.mode and both status codes in a dated hosting receipt that supersedes the conflicting README or receipt statement.

preregistration.expectation: The running dagu-equities service (127.0.0.1:18525) uses auth.mode none: an anonymous GET to its DAG-list API returns 200 and a GET carrying a dummy Basic header also returns 200. A loopback control instance of the same 2.16.6 binary with auth.mode basic (dummy generated credentials, disposable DAGU_HOME) returns 401 anonymous and 200 authenticated, proving the probe can detect basic auth.
preregistration.criteria: settled iff (a) the configured auth.mode line of the service's config is recorded without printing any other key, (b) both live status codes are recorded, (c) the control instance with auth.mode basic returns 401 anonymous and 200 authenticated and the control with auth.mode none returns 200 anonymous, all using the same curl command form, and (d) the hosting README gains a dated pointer to this receipt as superseding the 2026-09-19 basic-auth statement. Only GET requests reach the live service; it is never restarted or reconfigured.

results.fix_round_4: Loopback control with auth.mode none plus an auth.basic block: "server alive: no; exit status 1"; log: "Error: initialization error: failed to build config: auth.basic credentials are set but auth.mode is \"none\"; set auth.mode to 'basic' or remove the auth.basic section"; "stopped: port answers 000". Attempt 1's server.log holds the same error. So the hosting README's 'upstream rejects Basic credentials under none' is config validation of an auth.basic block, while request-level Basic headers under none are ignored (200 in rounds 1-3). Detection: had the server started, the script prints 'server alive: yes' and the status codes; the none control of rounds 1-3 started with the same config form minus the basic block.

limits: The configured mode is taken from the running server's own dashboard bootstrap (authMode) and its HTTP behavior; the private config.yaml was not read, to avoid reading any credential material. Under auth.mode none there is no credential, so the "authenticated" arm on the live service is a dummy Basic header, which upstream ignores.
Only GET requests reached the live service; it was not restarted or reconfigured (ExecMainStartTimestamp unchanged).

Controls used disposable DAGU_HOMEs on 127.0.0.1:18632/18633 with a random dummy password that was never printed; their config files were deleted after the run and both control servers were stopped (port answered 000).
Single host, single observation at 2026-09-23T05:19Z; the mode can change if the private config changes.
Fix round 4 checked config validation on the 2.16.6 binary only (the live service's version); the config-rejection behavior on 2.17.0 was not checked.

fixround4_preregistration.expectation: The pre-existing hosting README sentence 'upstream rejects Basic credentials under none' refers to configuration, not requests: a loopback dagu 2.16.6 control whose config has auth.mode none plus an auth.basic block either fails to start or logs a configuration error/warning, whereas request-level Basic headers under none are ignored (200, already observed in rounds 1-3).
fixround4_preregistration.criteria: The README wording is changed to whatever the control shows: if the server refuses to start or reports a config error, say config validation rejects an auth.basic block under none; if it starts silently, drop the 'rejects' claim and say only that request Basic headers are ignored under none. Either way the README states that request-level Basic headers are ignored under none. No change to the gap-2 outcome, which does not depend on this sentence. Detection: the control reports server exit status, whether the port answers, and greps its log for error/warn/basic lines.

preregistration_deviations: Criterion (a) required recording 'the configured auth.mode line of the service's config'. It was replaced, not met as written: the unit did not read the private config.yaml (it can hold credential material) and instead recorded the effective mode the running server serves in its dashboard bootstrap (authMode: "none"), corroborated by its HTTP behavior against controls that detect basic auth. The settled outcome rests on this substituted criterion; the literal config line remains unrecorded. The deviation was first stated explicitly in fix round 4 (second independent review).
